title: Words on a curve are typed on the curve and come in a letter at a time
goal: A headline set along a curve can be put there, reshaped and keyed, but re-wording it opens the words straight in a box until you finish, and a Reveal or a colour ramp does nothing to it. Let a person type the words in place on the curve and give curved words the same letter-by-letter reveals and ramps straight words have.
notes: Left from a-title-s-words-can-follow-a-curved-path (2026-10-18). Today: CanvasTextEditing opens the inline editor in the curve box with the words straight; DocumentRenderer skips reveal pieces when text.onPath != nil and InspectorPanel hides the Reveal section for curved words; TextRasterizer.rasterizeOnPath draws text.fillPaint flat (colorHex). Placement maths is TextOnPathLayout/PathWalk in PhotonzCore; TextRasterizer.pathLetters gives each glyph its place.
acceptance: Double-clicking words on a curve puts the caret on the curve and the letters stay on it while typing, as Illustrator types on a path
The Reveal section shows for words on a curve and a letter-at-a-time reveal brings each letter in where it stands on the curve, in the canvas, playback and an export
A colour ramp through the letters runs along the curve instead of being drawn flat
A walk at Next defaults proves all three, with a reel
